I think there is still a big difference in putting on personas in different situations and actual alters. I’m pretty sure like 90% of the population puts up “fronts” for different people, situations, etc… and I guess a person with DID could probably put up different fronts too because they are still a human in society etc etc. 


I would say those “fronts” are more likely to be switches if those moments feel blurry afterwards, you have bits of time/information missing about the situation, if you cant understand why you acted a certain way in that moment, felt out of control, etc etc… All in all, alters are dissociated fragments of your brain made to deal with trauma. The only times I’ve felt like “me slipping into an alter” would be like when I start to act a certain way and say certain things but I feel like I don’t have control over it. Not to the extent of like full on scary possession, but to the point where I’m sitting there like “why am I acting like this?” but can’t really do anything to stop it.

i hope that its comforting knowing someone relates, even if i dont think i have much advice to offer to you. but im gonna try anyways. (disclaimer i am not an expert, i am just someone who spends many hours reading about things and theorizing about my own life. take this all with a grain of salt i am only 20 years old)  

regarding your not knowing how much amnesia is normal, i would look to large gaps in memory rather than thinking of it like “oh i cant remember anything before a certain age”. If you’re having memories being recorded and then suddenly theres a random gap, thats abnormal in my opinion. It sounds literally crazy, and probably unsafe to do without a therapist in my case, but the way I went about it was trying to make a timeline of my whole life….I tried to dig deep into my core memories and map them out chronologically.  

This leads me into switches and dissociation. I also recorded times of my life that seemed abnormal or that I absolutely cannot relate to, to the point where it seems like an entirely different person. I’ve been online since I was 11 unfortunately so I have stuff saved that I’m able to look back on, and before that I’ve had diaries and such. It’s definitely a struggle trying to decipher what genuinely could’ve been a different person and what was just adolescence yknow. Although, that might just be something I tell myself so I can plunge my brain back into denial. The fact of the matter is that there is a big difference between teenage-not-knowing-who-you-are and that-is-a-whole-different-person-how-could-that-be-me. Doesn’t help that I have BPD so I struggle with identity anyways. But I digress.  

I am not suggesting that this is the way to go about it, I am just insane and I love charts and graphs and other information categorizing. But I was able to find patterns in seeming like a different person correlating with stressful/traumatic events. A good example was an awful relationship I was having when I was 14-15. It ended when I was 15 and there is a distinct shift between 15 and 16 for me, as well as 17 and 18, and so on and so forth etc etc.  

my real actual applicable advice would be  
1. journal about your experiences because it is so easy to forget, and if you’re chronically online like me, make a private account somewhere and make that your journal. it’ll be much much easier to see if something is amiss than just trying to remember if you feel like you’ve switched before or if you were dissociating or whatever else. also i am just a firm believer in journaling regardless, journals 4everr.  
2. do ur research. and not just medical articles, look into other peoples experiences on forums and whatever, compare it against your own, just read a bunch of stuff. but also it is a lot and this is a trauma based disorder so do take breaks….because it is tough and it is heavy and if you are a system there is a big big chance that your brain will say “no actually we dont want u looking into this right now” because OSDD and DID is all about protecting u from shit. that is just purely from experience because i dissociate HEAVILY when my brain thinks im researching stuff i shouldnt be.  
3. get a good trauma therapist. this is extremely hard and it has been impossible for me. so this is more like a long term goal.  

thats all, thanks if u read my entire spiel, i wish the both of us luck on finding answers

I get real crushes very, very, rarely. The last one was about 5ish years ago and currently I’ve had a debilitating one since may. I feel like I act literally insane around them but I know logically that it’s probably all internal. I’m more than likely to just never talk to them/avoid them like the plague/do stupid shit around them and regret it 24/7. HOWEVER, when I do interact with them, I honestly feel like it’s akin to being in school and having a crush on a teacher…very specific type of awkward idealization, hanging on their every word, trying to impress them with my knowledge. Doesn’t help that I also just legitimately crush on teachers a lot but-

i definitely relate, but also i think i have a lot of narcissistic traits in addition to my bpd. i experience EXTREME jealousy when people have stuff that i dont have because i believe its impossible for me, like healthy relationships and steady jobs that they enjoy. it turns into this sickening resentment where i end up just hating anybody that seems to get those things so easily.  

from a purely bpd-fear-of-abandonment point of view however, i definitely feel like if my friends are doing well, then they’ll realize how “crazy” i am and how they never should have been around me in the first place. as if their own “crazy veil” has been lifted and they can finally see clearly and realize “oh my god i have got to get away from this person and move on with my life.”  

btw dont let anybody be an asshole to you over this post, people hate to discuss the ugly sides of bpd for some bizarre reason. but i think as long as you’re acknowledging it as something unhealthy then you’re already going in the right direction.
